text:
anya: FYI I ran a quick nsys capture on the 8-GPU shard during the tensor-parallel rollout. capture id gpuprod_2026_01_12.nsys
matt: link? also paste the CLI you used
anya: ran `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,cublas,nccl -f true -o /tmp/gpuprod` on the serve node during a 30s steady-state QPS test (seq=1024, batch=16). flamegraph attached in my gdrive.
raj: quick summary of what I saw: big all-reduce spikes at iteration boundaries, NCCL latency ~1.2ms per ~256MB reduce, and compute idle time ~18% between kernels.
anya: timeline shows overlap windows are tiny. allreduce frequently executes on the default stream which forces sync with subsequent kernels.
matt: could be we're using blocking `ncclAllReduce` on the wrong stream. are we passing a dedicated comm stream per tensor?
anya: no explicit comm stream in the wrapper. snippet is basically:
```cpp
// pseudo
cudaStream_t s = defaultStream;
ncclAllReduce(send, recv, count, ncclFloat32, ncclSum, comm, s);
```
matt: that will serialize. try creating a per-comm stream and enqueue the allreduce there, then use `cudaEventRecord` + `cudaStreamWaitEvent` to sync only when needed to consume results.
raj: also noticed kernel selection falling back to cublasGemm for small K in matmul -> higher kernel launch overhead. switching to a fused matmul/epilogue or cublasLt shaved ~6-9% utilization in the trace.
anya: KV cache behaviour: cold-cache fills cause big variance in GPU memory traffic and kernel footprints. warm runs (cache hit) had ~12% better wall time for long-context requests. worth instrumenting cache hit/miss in the trace.
matt: there's also a perf regression repro: master @abcdef3 shipped a new batching heuristic that naively packs variable sequence lengths. that increases variance of allreduce sizes which spikes NCCL.
anya: suggestion for repro: run a synthetic workload with controlled seq-length histogram, e.g. {64:40%, 512:40%, 1024:20%} and measure allreduce byte-size distribution and p99 latency.
perf-bot: perf-alert: 2026-02-03 14:22 — +8.4% regression in p99 latency on dedicated-gpu cluster (automated test 'dedicated_inference_longctx').
raj: for observability we should add per-collective microtimers: record start_event on comm stream before nccl call and end_event after completion, and emit nelapsed + bytes. also track overlap ratio = compute_time / (compute_time + comm_time).
matt: I'll add a small wrapper around NCCL calls that emits `rpc_perf.collective` events (nccl_bytes, nccl_ms, stream_id). debug-only flag `--perf-collect=collective` so we don't flood prod.
anya: can we also sample nsys with `--sample` on a subset of requests so we can correlate trace ids with per-collective timers?
raj: yes, attach an nvtx range with the request id and the collective id. nsys will show the NVTX ranges and we can map to our microtimers for validation.
matt: ops to try in experiments: 1) move allreduce to dedicated comm stream + events, 2) enable cublasLt fallback for small GEMMs, 3) test batching heuristic pinned packing (pad vs concat) to reduce variability, 4) run NCCL env toggles `NCCL_ALGO=RING` / `TREE`, and `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` to isolate IB issues.
anya: I'll run experiment 3 and 4 on a staging 8xA100 cluster and post traces. raj pls run nsight captures for experiment 1. matt pls add the microtimer PR.
raj: quick note: when collecting nsys, capture at least 30s steady-state so the KV cache warm-up isn't dominating the profile. also capture per-GPU SM util and achieved occupancy.
matt: ack, I'll open a small PR to add the wrapper and toggle. aim to have it in a feature branch by EOD tomorrow.
anya: thanks — if we can get per-collective histograms and a couple nsight captures we'll be able to quantify overlap gains. :rocket:
raj: ack
matt: ack
anya: rough timeline: collect traces today, microtimer PR tomorrow, run full synthetic sweep Wed.
anya: pinging @eng-sre later for a scheduled low-impact capture window so we don't disturb traffic.
